_comment: AXBeat's editorial layer, and the only place display copy for a row lives.
The scan in ax-audit is the authority on every score, host and check: nothing
here can change a number. What lives here is the two things a scan cannot know.
name  what a reader calls the chain. L2Beat's entry names carry qualifiers
('Arbitrum One', 'OP Mainnet', 'ZKsync Era') that read as noise in a
ranked list. The scan keeps the full name; the board shows this one.
note  why a row is not the obvious host, written for a visitor rather than
for us. The targets file has its own notes, but those explain a scanning
decision to the person running the scan. A note is only written here when
a reader would otherwise mistrust the row (a rebrand, a cross-host
redirect, a chain with no site of its own).
logo  path to the chain's mark, vendored into axbeat-logos/ (never hotlinked).
Sourced from L2Beat's icon set (l2beat.com/icons/<slug>.png), downscaled
to 40x40 (2x a 20px display size) and verified by eye against the brand
it claims to be. Required for every brand: there is no per-chain fallback,
so a brand added to the scan without an entry here ships with a broken img.
Keyed by the `brand` in ax-audit's targets file. A brand in the scan with no
entry here ships under its own name with no note, which is the common case.
scripts/axbeat-data.mjs fails the build if an entry here matches no brand in
the scan, so a rename upstream cannot leave a stale note behind.

Morph.note: Morph moved to morph.network during 2026; the old morphl2.io address redirects there.

Unichain.note: The docs address redirects to Uniswap’s developer portal, so the docs score belongs to Uniswap’s site, not one Unichain runs.

INTMAX.note: Docs scored at docs.network.intmax.io, the address INTMAX links to. docs.intmax.io does not resolve.

Honeypot v2.note: Scanned as Cartesi (cartesi.io and docs.cartesi.io). Honeypot v2 is Cartesi’s bug-bounty chain and has no site of its own.
